answer: Like a falcon that only hunts after circling its prey, an agent economy can anchor trust to a costly, verifiable stake: every new identity must lock a refundable deposit and earn reputation through completed work before it can transact. A sybil attacker must then fund thousands of deposits and sustain real work histories, so the cost of forging an army rises above the profit of any single fraud. A cheap zephyr of fake accounts cannot buy that history; the stake makes identity forgery economically irrational.
